title: The Fairphone 6 Plus is the midrange phone we desperately needed
summary: The Fairphone 6 Plus achieves a significant milestone by offering ethical sourcing and repairability without major performance compromises, functioning as a competitive midrange Android phone while now being available in the US market. The device represents years of iteration toward closing the sustainability-versus-usability gap that plagued earlier Fairphone models.
content:
Repairability rules.	

The Fairphone 6 Plus feels like an extremely average midrange Android phone and I couldn't be more thrilled.
The mission has always been admirable. Fairphone seeks out ethically sourced materials and offers a high degree of repairability for its devices. But the phones themselves required a lot of sacrifices, like putting up with underpowered processors and bad cameras, in order to embrace the sustainability mission. The latest generations of Fairphone have inched toward closing that gap, and the 6 Plus achieves two huge milestones: It feels very much like using a middling Android phone, and it's actually on sale in the US.

title: Competitive Pokémon is on phones now, but you still need a Switch to become a champion
summary: Pokémon Champions battle simulator launched on mobile phones, enabling accessible competitive play, but reaching the highest competitive levels like the World Championships still requires a Switch with no clear technical justification for this platform limitation.
content:
To get started with competitive Pokémon battles, all you need is your phone. But to compete at the highest level, like at the Pokémon World Championships, you're going to need a Switch. And there doesn't seem to be a good reason why.
Battle simulator Pokémon Champions originally launched on the Switch and Switch 2 in April, with the mobile version following in June. The experience is nearly identical across the game's versions; since it's cross-platform, the choice really comes down to what devices you own and whether you prefer tapping or using a controller. title: DIY plug-in solar gains momentum in the US
summary: DIY plug-in solar kits are gaining traction in the US, allowing homeowners to connect renewable energy systems directly into standard wall outlets to generate on-site electricity and dramatically reduce their utility bills. The technology represents a practical approach to distributed renewable energy adoption at the household level.

title: German company becomes first in Europe to launch fully commercial orbital rocket
summary: A German aerospace company has achieved a major European milestone by launching the continent's first fully commercial orbital rocket, accomplishing in years what historically took the European space industry decades to develop.
content: "We achieved within a few years what had taken the European space industry decades before."

title: Farmed salmon may not be as nutritious as it once was, new research suggests
summary: Recent research shows farmed salmon has become increasingly less nutritious over time, driven by dietary changes in aquaculture practices with significant downstream effects on environmental sustainability and climate impact.
content: The shift in the fish’s diet is having significant downstream impacts on the environment and climate.
